A construction worker who was driving with more than twice the legal limit of alcohol in his system when he crashed his truck, killing another man and injuring four others, was sentenced to 12 years in prison Thursday. Alfonso Estrada-Salinas, 35, pleaded guilty to intoxication manslaughter and intoxication assault in the June 27, 2024, deadly drunken driving incident in Bellmead. Judge Susan Kelly of Waco's 54th State District Court accepted the plea bargain, which called for Estrada-Salinas to be sentenced to concurrent prison sentences of 12 years and 10 years. He must serve at least six years in prison before he can seek parole. Department of Public Safety officials said Estrada-Salinas admitted to drinking nine to 12 beers during the day after missing a turn about 7:15 p.m. and crashing his truck into a tree on Katy Lane near Preston Lane in Bellmead. Eduardo Soto Salaices, 20, of Durango, Mexico, was pronounced dead at the scene. DPS officials said four other passengers in the pickup were treated at a Waco hospital, one with critical injuries and the other three with non-life-threatening injuries. There were multiple open and unopened alcoholic beverages in the vehicle at the crash scene, according to arrest records. Estrada-Salinas has been held under bonds totaling $100,000 and an immigration detainer since his arrest.
